title: The Mixtape of the water tower
premise: When Tamsin Underhill transfers to Marrow Creek High, they discover the school's beloved senior tradition—the Mixtape, a cassette passed down since 1979 and played from the old water tower each spring—hums with something more than nostalgia: the town's founding families literally stored their memories in it, feeding on the town's devotion. The college essay prompt 'What will you leave behind?' cracks the tape open, and Tamsin begins hearing voices that aren't theirs. As graduation nears, the tape starts consuming students' futures to sustain itself, and Tamsin must decide whether to destroy the tradition that built the town or rewrite it—ultimately recording their own honest voice over the founders' stolen ones, freeing the town at the cost of being forgotten by everyone they saved.
about_author: Elodie Eastwick grew up in a mill town where the water tower was the tallest thing for fifty miles, and she has never stopped wondering what it heard. She writes stories about small towns with long memories and teenagers who refuse to inherit them quietly.

chapters.title: Head Down, Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Three weeks into Marrow Creek High, Tamsin has perfected invisibility—until English class assigns the senior essay prompt, 'What will you leave behind?' Watching golden-boy Deacon Reyes brag about playing next year's Mixtape from the tower, Tamsin feels the first strange pull of curiosity. Beat: wary belonging, the ache of starting over.

chapters.title: The Prompt That Answers Back
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Drafting the essay alone at night, Tamsin writes one true sentence about leaving nothing behind—and hears it whispered back in a voice like rusted metal. The library's locked archive case holds the original 1979 cassette, warm to the touch. Beat: dread braided with fascination; the hook sets.

chapters.title: Side A: The Founders' Voices
chapters.summary: Tamsin and reluctant lab partner Priya Nair sneak into the archive and play the tape: six founding-family voices narrating the town's history—but describing events that haven't happened yet. Priya, whose family name is on the tower plaque, goes pale. Beat: wonder curdling into fear as memory reveals itself as machinery.

chapters.title: Tradition Is Just Power Wearing a Letterman Jacket
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV. Deacon rehearses his ceremonial climb, desperate to escape his father's shadow as a Reyes founder-descendant. He notices seniors who've 'given their verse' to the tape drifting through school hollow-eyed, futures oddly pre-written. He dismisses it—until he finds his own name already recorded. Beat: complicity awakening into doubt.

chapters.title: What the Tower Keeps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Following the whispers to the decommissioned pump house, Tamsin finds the truth: the founders bound their memories into the tape to outlive death, and every playback feeds them the town's tomorrows. The tape offers Tamsin a bargain—belonging, forever, in exchange for a verse. Beat: temptation made personal.

chapters.title: Static Between Friends
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya wants to expose the tape; her grandmother, a founder's daughter, begs her not to—the tradition 'made' their family. When Priya records her refusal, the tape takes her scholarship acceptance letter instead, rewriting her future mid-sentence. Beat: betrayal by inheritance; stakes turn intimate and irreversible.

chapters.title: The Longest Side B
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With two weeks to graduation, the tape grows hungry, taking verses from half the senior class. Tamsin and Deacon form an uneasy alliance, decoding the founders' binding ritual in the 1979 liner notes: the tape can be overwritten, but only from the tower, only by someone willing to give up what they'd leave behind. Beat: resolve forged under countdown pressure.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Goodbye
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The night before the ceremony, Tamsin records a practice overwrite—and the founders fight back, flooding Tamsin's mind with every borrowed memory until identity frays. Priya anchors them with a list of things worth forgetting nothing for. Beat: darkest hour; the cost becomes fully known and accepted.

chapters.title: Climb
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV, then shared. During the spring ceremony, before the whole town, Deacon stalls the ritual while Tamsin climbs the tower with a boombox and a blank tape. The founders scream through the speakers; the crowd hears its own stolen years played back. Tamsin presses record on one honest voice. Beat: public climax, sacrifice in full light.

chapters.title: What You Leave Behind
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, epilogue. The new Mixtape plays only human voices—grief, hope, ordinary futures returned. The town remembers a tradition but not the kid who freed it; Tamsin walks the halls a stranger, at peace. In the essay Tamsin finally submits: 'I left behind my name, and kept everything else.' Beat: bittersweet resolution, inheritance rewritten.
